title: Money
status: draft: written 18 Nov 2026 offline for Grade 8; not yet checked by a Kenyan maths teacher; not loaded by the live tutor
notes: Official outcomes a to e are tested; f (use IT) and g (spend responsibly) are not questions. Simple interest is I = P × R × T / 100 with the time in years. Compound interest, appreciation and depreciation are worked step by step, year by year, up to three years, as the design says (no formula with a power). Hire purchase compares the deposit plus all the instalments with the cash price. The compound interest families carry the HOREB skills G8_SIMPLE_INTEREST and G9_COMPOUND_INTEREST and the depreciation and hire purchase families G8_PROFIT_LOSS; all are kept. Teacher to confirm: the SACCO and chama contexts, and whether finding the rate or time from simple interest (no family yet) is taught in Grade 8.

skills.key_step: The child points at the principal first and says interest is only the extra on top.

floor.prerequisite: Finds a percentage of an amount.
floor.question: 8% of 20,000

steps: Find the money put in or borrowed: principal.
Rate is per cent a year; time is in years.
contexts: a loan for a posho mill

board.do: Draw a bar of 20,000 and a small piece of 1,600 on the end.
Point at the small piece.
Wait for the child to say interest.
Point at the whole bar.

misconceptions.ask: Is that what she put in or the extra?
Does that include what she put in?
What does 8% mean?
Who is using whose money?

checks.question: Amina saves 30,000 and gets back 33,000. The interest?
In the same story, what is the principal?

skills.key_step: The child writes P, R and T with T in years before putting them into I = PRT/100.
representations: a table year by year with the same interest
contexts: a bank loan for a matatu

board.do: Draw a table with three years, each earning 1,600.
Point at the three 1,600s.
Wait for 4,800.

misconceptions.ask: Can the interest be more than the loan?
Is that for one year or three?
Is 6 months 6 years?
Interest or amount?

checks.question: Simple interest on 15,000 shillings at 6% a year for 4 years?
The amount on 24,000 shillings at 5% a year for 9 months?

skills.key_step: The child finds the interest for one year first, then compares it with the principal.

board.do: Write: 15,000 grows to 18,000 in 2 years.
Point at 18,000.
board.say: How much of this is interest?

board.do: Wait for 3,000.
Ask: how much interest in one year?

misconceptions.ask: Is the principal smaller than the interest?
Is 18,000 the interest?
Is the rate a per cent?
Is 3,000 for one year?

checks.question: 20,000 shillings earns 4,000 shillings simple interest in 4 years. Rate?
At 8% a year, 12,000 shillings earns 2,880 shillings. How many years?

skills.key_step: The child writes the amount at the start of each year on its own line and works that year's interest on it.

floor.prerequisite: Finds simple interest for one year.
floor.question: 10% of 11,000

representations: a SACCO table row by row
steps: Year 1: interest on the principal; add it.
Year 2: interest on the new amount; add it.

board.do: Draw a table: year, start, interest, end.
The child fills year 1: 10,000, 1,000, 11,000.
Point at the start of year 2.
Wait for 11,000.

misconceptions.ask: Is year 2 interest on 10,000 or 11,000?
How many years?
Is that all the money?
How much is in the account at the start of year 2?
How much did they put in?
Is the interest the whole amount?
What rate does each pay?
Is simple interest paid every year?
What is the interest worked on?

checks.question: 20,000 shillings at 10% compound interest for 2 years. Amount?
10,000 shillings at 10% compound for 3 years. Interest earned?

skills.key_step: The child takes the percentage off the value at the start of each year and sees the fall getting smaller.
representations: a table of value by year
steps: Year 1: take r% of the price off.
Year 2: take r% of the new value off.
Answer the value or the loss as asked.

board.do: Draw a table: year, value at start, loss, value at end.
The child fills year 1 for 120,000 at 20%.
Point at the start of year 2.
Wait for the child to predict.

misconceptions.ask: Year 2: 20% of which value?
How many years?
Lost or left?
Is the fall the same amount each year?
What is 20% of 25,600?
After year 1, is the phone worth more or less?
misconceptions.repair: Less: the second loss is smaller.

misconceptions.ask: Does a phone keep getting older?
Are both taken from the same price?

checks.question: A motorcycle of 150,000 shillings loses 10% a year. Value after 2 years?
A phone of 20,000 shillings loses 25% a year. Value after 3 years?

skills.key_step: The child adds the percentage of the value at the start of each year, and first says whether the item gains or loses value.
representations: a table of value by year
steps: Year 1: add r% of the value.
Year 2: add r% of the new value.
Answer the value or the gain.

board.do: Draw two columns: gains value, loses value.
The child puts land, a phone, a car and a plot in the columns.
Point at land.
board.say: If it gains 10% a year, what is 500,000 worth after a year?

board.do: Wait for 550,000.

misconceptions.ask: Does appreciate mean up or down?
Year 2: 10% of which value?
Gain or value?
Is a two-year-old phone worth more than a new one?

checks.question: Land worth 800,000 shillings appreciates 5% a year. Value after 2 years?
A plot worth 1,000,000 gains 10% a year. Gain after 3 years?

skills.key_step: The child writes deposit + number × instalment as the hire purchase total before comparing with anything.
steps: To compare plans, find each total.
Say which is cheaper and by how much.
contexts: a television in a Nairobi shop

board.do: Draw a poster: cash 21,000, or deposit 5,000 and 10 × 2,000.
Point at the instalments.
board.say: How much are all ten together?

board.do: Wait for 20,000.
The child adds the deposit and compares with the cash price.

misconceptions.ask: Is that the extra or the total?
What did she pay altogether?
What did she pay on the first day?
What does each plan cost in total?
Add up the payments: more or less than cash?

checks.question: Cash price 40,000. Hire purchase: deposit 8,000 and 12 instalments of 3,000. How much more?
Plan A: deposit 3,000 and 6 × 2,500. Plan B: deposit 5,000 and 4 × 3,000. Cheaper plan?
